context: Recorded by MB-66 (lane R). Operator approval: ~/Buildo-scratch/p2close/CARD-wave0-approval.answered.md ("approve all recommendations", sections B and C) and CARD-local-db.answered.md. Plan ~/Buildo-scratch/mcbylaws/MB-66/aj3/plan-al.md.

decisions.subject: S-1: M-404
decisions.recommendation: Cards S-1 (CARD-plan-1030-approval) and wave0 section B; research Q1. Rule text: S-1 storey conversion values are logic variables, each seeded with its citation by MB-31 into scripts/seeds/logic_variables.json (these variables are absent today) and changed only by a ruling: s1_ceiling_min_m = 2.3 (Ontario Building Code 2024, Part 9, Table 9.5.3.1, living, dining and kitchen space, over at least 75 % of the area); s1_floor_assembly_m = 0.212 (joist 184 mm, Table 9.23.4.2.-A, plus subfloor 15.5 mm, Table 9.23.15.5.-A, plus ceiling board 12.7 mm, Table 9.29.5.3, which sum to 212.2 mm; finished floor and furring are 0 and disclosed as not cited); s1_parapet_m = 0.3 (10.20.40.10(5)). Floor-to-floor f = s1_ceiling_min_m + s1_floor_assembly_m (2.512 m); roof allowance a = s1_floor_assembly_m + s1_parapet_m (one assembly plus 0.3 m, 0.512 m); storeys = floor((height - a) / f) where M-391 lets S-1 apply. The 184 mm joist is a disclosed design choice, and the 0.3 m parapet governs RD main wall height only, so its use for building height is a disclosed extension.

decisions.subject: S-2: M-405
decisions.recommendation: Card S-2 (queue O-4); wave0 section B "S-2 = 0, disclosed". Rule text: S-2 first-floor height above established grade is the logic variable s2_first_floor_above_grade_m = 0, to be seeded by MB-31 into scripts/seeds/logic_variables.json (absent today) and disclosed as an assumption: the first floor is taken at established grade, no by-law first-floor height is applied, and S-2 is subtracted from the height before S-1 converts it, so with 0 it changes no result; it changes only by a ruling.

decisions.subject: MB18-RL-3: M-406
decisions.recommendation: MB18-RL-3 (47,779 parcels, including A0067, have depth and length not_evaluated without it). Rule text: Phase 2 stays strict (Spec 134 I10, inputs_defaulted = 0); the one addition is a disclosed site-fact assumption, "the lot is unchanged since 2013" (the 569-2013 enactment), resolved per design option (M-400) and never stored as a defaulted input: with it a lot whose exception keys a minimum as existing(lot_frontage_m; enacted(569-2013)) reads its stored frontage as the 2013 frontage, flagged and disclosed in the M-169 manner, and Spec 134 I10 does not count that assumption as a defaulted input.

decisions.subject: MB18-RL-1: M-407
decisions.recommendation: MB18-RL-1 (the code is right; the LC-68 wording is clarified). Rule text: Spec 131 LC-68 is clarified and the code stands: a "4-vertex lot" in LC-68 means a lot whose stored outline holds 4 points; the outline is a closed ring, so 4 points is 3 corners, a triangle with no rear lot line (no_rear_lot_line = true, as pull-golden-lots.cjs and scripts/lib/bylaw-resolution.js already set it), while a four-sided lot stores 5 points and keeps its rear lot line; "other shapes are flagged" means the lots of other shapes are listed by their stored point count (measured on the local database 2026-10-30: 719 parcels store 4 points, 165,832 store 5), not marked with a stored flag.

decisions.subject: MB18-RL-2: M-408
decisions.recommendation: MB18-RL-2 (SC-14 has no detector until the term is defined). Rule text: A rule-choice branch (the thing Spec 68 SC-14 counts) is a literal equal to a zone symbol (R, RD, RS, RT, RM) or to a building-type token, in an executable position in a file of the Layer 2 closure; the detector is report-only first, with measured baseline 0.

decisions.subject: MB18-RL-4: M-409
decisions.recommendation: MB18-RL-4 (close form for RB-D10). Rule text: RB-D10 is closed by removing only value.ratio of the audit row whose metric is storage_within_budget from the compared golden, scoped by audit metric, never as a band and never through the volatile-keys list; the budget check itself still reads MiB, the ledger row stays OPEN until the night recapture, and the change needs a second-seat check and a decision-log line because it touches a golden comparison (a protected path).

decisions.subject: MB18-RL-5: M-410
decisions.recommendation: MB18-RL-5 (who edits the one lineage line). Rule text: If another lane already holds docs/reference/maxbld-field-lineage.json, the MB-18 claim still edits the one lineage line for front_setback_fallback_m (item (j)) under that lane's agreement, in the same commit as the Layer 2 scope entry, the migration and the lock tests; without that line the both-ways lineage lock cannot go green.

decisions.subject: MB30-PR-1: M-368 note
decisions.recommendation: MB30-PR-1 (the restore UPDATE would stamp updated_at on permits). Rule text: M-368's "the tables it restores" includes a table whose SET NULL reference column the restore writes (night 3: permits.neighbourhood_id, whose triggers set_updated_at, trg_permits_lead_id and trg_permits_set_location would otherwise fire), not only the backed-up tables; permit work itself stays out of scope.

decisions.subject: MB30-PR-2: M-368 note
decisions.recommendation: MB30-PR-2 (what the dump is). Rule text: A Layer 2 night's "dump first" (F-22, F-44) is the night tool's table snapshot (n3db backup-sql, verified equal to live) of the night's declared write set plus its CASCADE closure, the only snapshot the M-368 restore can restore; a full database dump (Spec 112) is an optional extra, never the restore source.

decisions.subject: MB30-PR-4: M-368 note
decisions.recommendation: MB30-PR-4 (nightD restore; yes in principle, no build until a trigger exists). Rule text: "Every night restore" in M-368 includes nightD's own restore (TRUNCATE of bylaw_resolution_lots, bylaw_resolution_texts and bylaw_resolution_units, then \copy), in principle: no change is made for it until one of those tables carries a user trigger (none does on 2026-10-30), and then the same per-table DISABLE TRIGGER USER wrapper applies.

decisions.subject: MB30-S112: Spec 112 4.3 note
decisions.recommendation: MB30 Spec 112 section 4.3 one-line note. Rule text: Spec 112 section 4.3 allows the wrapper M-368 needs: a per-table ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER USER (table owner) inside the restore transaction, re-enabled before commit; pg_restore --disable-triggers and DISABLE TRIGGER ALL stay not used.

decisions.subject: LOCAL-DB: R-LR
decisions.recommendation: CARD-local-db (MB30-PR-3 and "the cloud needs to wait"). Rule text: The only database any McBylaws work reads or writes is the local database at 127.0.0.1:54322 (the local Supabase container); the cloud waits: no McBylaws lane runs a cloud:* script, or connects to, reads, writes, migrates or deploys to a remote or production database, until the operator rules otherwise in a later card, and a script whose target is not 127.0.0.1:54322 stops. This also settles MB30-PR-3: the dev DB is the local database.

decisions.subject: MB64-PR-1: M-411
decisions.recommendation: MB64-PR-1 (lane default). Rule text: The increment-1 loop data and tests live under src/tests/mcbylaws/loop/increment-1/**, src/tests/mcbylaws/pending/increment-1/** and src/tests/mcbylaws/loop/seam.ts (none exists today); every file stays in pending/ until MB-31 passes it and is run by path; mcbylaws/protected-paths.json (to be built by MB-67) lists all three globs.

decisions.subject: MB64-PR-2: M-412
decisions.recommendation: MB64-PR-2 (changes numbers: 24 step-2 fronts, 21 footprints, 10 GFAs and A0578). Rule text: In increment 1 the whole front-yard chain (M-387) and the corner lot's street-side side-yard term are computed, as the newest dated queue line says; the older queue lines that place street-side and averaging in increment 2 are overridden by this row; the cells that rest on this choice are marked provisional and kept out of the floors.

decisions.subject: MB64-PR-3: M-413
decisions.recommendation: MB64-PR-3 (changes numbers: several 17 m depths). Rule text: For increment 1 the footprint depth axis reads building_length_m in the same min() as building_depth_m, exactly as Guardrail G-1 is printed in the queue; the width-axis rule is revisited when the options increment is reached.

decisions.subject: MB64-PR-4: M-414
decisions.recommendation: MB64-PR-4 (strict; A0553 is the only lot with a same-street neighbour excluded on distance). Rule text: Front-yard step 2 uses only a neighbour that is on the same street, residential, estimated and whose building is 15.0 m or less from the lot (10.5.40.70(1)), the abutting-building tokens are read from parcel_abutments (M-245), and user figures are bounded by fya_est_min_m and fya_est_max_m; the strict reading holds: where (A) "beside one lot" fails because the second lot beside the subject lot has its building beyond 15.0 m and (B) "between two abutting lots" needs both, averaging does not apply and step 4, the zone value Phase 2 stores, answers, so A0553 stays not_evaluated until MB-18 item (j) stores front_setback_fallback_m; three or more qualifying neighbours stay as M-245 (Q-B2).

decisions.subject: MB64-PR-5: M-415
decisions.recommendation: MB64-PR-5 (lane default). Rule text: MB-31 exposes the seam runRow(rowId, inputs) returning {status, value, reason, flags[], trace[]}, and the McBylaws loop reaches Layer 3 only through it (src/tests/mcbylaws/loop/seam.ts, to be built by MB-64); the rounding contract is an area tolerance of 0.005 and a tie tolerance of 1e-9.

decisions.subject: MB64-PR-7: M-416
decisions.recommendation: MB64-PR-7 (lane default). Rule text: In the applicant comparison a notice's figures are compared only when its type reads as a detached house or as an addition to an existing detached house or dwelling, and not as semi-detached, houseplex, apartment or suite; any other type is recorded as not_scored:type_not_comparable.

decisions.subject: MB64-PR-8: M-417
decisions.recommendation: MB64-PR-8 (lane default). Rule text: Increment 1 reads the permission word only for the detached house: required_lot_area_m2 and required_lot_frontage_m, named in the queue's permitted row, are not stored by Phase 2 for it, so permitted is provisional and stays out of the floors.

decisions.subject: MB64-PR-9: M-418
decisions.recommendation: MB64-PR-9 (lane default; checked on the local database 2026-10-30). Rule text: The variables fya_porch_allowance_m and the four fya_placeholder_* are in scripts/seeds/logic_variables.json but only fya_est_min_m and fya_est_max_m are in the local logic_variables table; MB-31 applies the rest from the answered FS-SB1 and FS-SB2 cards and seeds footprint_shape_factor at 1.0 with the shape switch off (LC-69); the queue line that says the fya_* variables already exist is corrected by this row.

decisions.subject: MB64-PR-10: M-419
decisions.recommendation: MB64-PR-10 (14 of the 25 cases are unlimited). Rule text: A Phase 2 height_storeys of unlimited means no Phase 2 cap, so the S-1 arithmetic gives the storeys (M-391, M-399); an unlimited storey value is never used as the storeys term of GFA.

decisions.subject: MB64-PR-12: M-420
decisions.recommendation: MB64-PR-12 (absent target, not an undecided cell). Rule text: A principal-structure gfa_m2 target that Phase 2 does not store (only the suites have one) is an absent target: it drops out of the GFA minimum and does not make the GFA not_evaluated; M-385 applies to a stored undecided cell only.

decisions.subject: MB64-PR-13: M-421
decisions.recommendation: MB64-PR-13 (parcel 10 corners, keyed golden 9). Rule text: The corner flag the scorer reads is the parcel layer's (O-13), the keyed golden or FS-Q3 flag is shown beside it, and the parcel flag is to be fixed by MB-18 or the keying lane (A0562 is a ruled corner) before the cases are re-run.

decisions.subject: P67-1: R-KV
decisions.recommendation: R-KH names rules[] but not where they live. Rule text: A Layer 2/3 commit names its task in one trailer line McBylaws-Task: MB-nn, and the task's pre-registered rules[] live in its prereg file scripts/analysis/bylaw-validation/coa-expected/prereg-[MB-id]-[round].json (schema coa-round-prereg-v1; MB-68 owns the schema and the writer, MB-67 adds the single field task and only reads task and rules[]); the gate reads the newest prereg whose task equals the trailer from the commit's parent tree, never the index; one file per task; the commit that creates a prereg, with that prereg as its only Layer 2/3 path and no cited rules, needs no trailer.

decisions.subject: P67-2: R-KW
decisions.recommendation: R-KK cannot run in CI on an untracked file. Rule text: .cursor/MCBYLAWS-QUEUE.md is a tracked file on wf1/mb-rulings (it is untracked today), committed by the orchestrator before the queue check is wired; each DONE entry is written MB-nn@sha and never rewritten; lane branches enter by merge, not rebase.

decisions.subject: P67-3: R-KX
decisions.recommendation: R-KP names no branch or content. Rule text: The hold file is mcbylaws/APPROVED at the repo root of the McBylaws base branch wf1/mb-rulings (absent today): it counts only if git cat-file -e HEAD:mcbylaws/APPROVED succeeds, its first line matches ^O-1 APPROVED [0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}, and the commit that adds it touches no other path; it must be present in the parent tree of each Layer 2/3 commit, checked commit by commit and not at the tip; the rule applies only when the staged set holds a Layer 2/3 path; the pre-push summary prints its commit id, date and subject first whenever it changes.

decisions.subject: P67-4: R-KY
decisions.recommendation: R-KP names no mechanism. Rule text: Pre-push approval is an interactive prompt on /dev/tty ("Approve this push? [y/N]") after the summary, and only when the push changes a protected path; no tty, no answer, or anything but y refuses; a push that touches no protected path prints one line and passes; in CI the summary is printed to the log and the arms run with no prompt.

decisions.subject: P67-5: R-KZ
decisions.recommendation: M-381 gives no search key. Rule text: The conflict search of M-381 runs over the 69a, 124a and 131 register rows with two keys: every clause token in the new row's text, and every pair of a building type and a subject word taken from closed lists; the new row's Conflict check names every id the search returns, each followed by no conflict (with the reason), amends or supersedes.

decisions.subject: P67-6: R-LA
decisions.recommendation: R-KR widens scope without listing files. Rule text: The literal gate (R-KN) covers the files in the literal_scope of mcbylaws/protected-paths.json (to be built by MB-67): the Layer 3 step, evaluator-extension and helper files that MB-31 names, and the JSON data modules among them; it also covers every new or changed line in scripts/analysis/bylaw/evaluate.mjs and the Layer 2 closure files, whose number literals existing on 2026-10-30 (61 in evaluate.mjs outside 0, 1, 2 and 100) are a shrink-only baseline in mcbylaws/literal-allow.json, so R-KR is not narrowed; strings are allowed only from mcbylaws/literal-allow.json (absent today; status_words[] and field_names[]), a protected path whose every change appears in the pre-push summary.

decisions.subject: P67-7: R-LB
decisions.recommendation: R-DJ (2) budgets cover docs-only and registry commits only. Rule text: The Layer 2/3 gate is one more && line in .husky/pre-commit, measured by scripts/analysis/precommit-budget.mjs --measure and kept inside the R-DJ (2) budgets with a re-pinned evidence file (R-EC --check is red until it is re-measured); the MB-68 fast loop set runs only when Layer 2/3 files are staged and is outside the docs-only and registry timings.

decisions.subject: P67-8: R-LC
decisions.recommendation: R-KM names the file but not its content. Rule text: The minimum panel record is docs/reports/panels/[task].json (absent today), a JSON file with task (equal to the trailer), class (the queue class letter), plan (a non-empty array of seats) and output (a non-empty array of seats); the roster per class is MB-73's audit, not the gate's.

decisions.subject: P67-9: R-LD
decisions.recommendation: F-34 and R-KP do not list the gate's own files. Rule text: The protected paths (R-KP) include, beyond the F-34 list: mcbylaws/APPROVED, mcbylaws/protected-paths.json and mcbylaws/literal-allow.json (the mcbylaws/ directory is absent today), docs/reports/panels/** and docs/reports/loop-records/** (both absent today), .husky/*, .github/workflows/test.yml, scripts/lib/exec-policy.json, the gate's ground truth (Specs 133, 69a, 124a and 131) and the gate's own tests, fixtures and docs/reports/generated/precommit-budget.json; every change to any of them appears in the pre-push summary.

decisions.subject: P67-10: R-LE
decisions.recommendation: Without (a) and (b) the first prereg and the APPROVED commit deadlock. Rule text: The gate does not refuse the commits that authorise it: (a) a commit whose only Layer 2/3 path is one valid prereg file and which cites no rules is exempt from the trailer and rules[] checks; (b) the hold applies only when a Layer 2/3 path is staged, so the operator's sole APPROVED commit (R-KX) passes; and RULED means the closed list of in-force Status words the generator emits (RETIRED, SUPERSEDED, PROPOSED and OWED are not RULED); BOOT-1 stays the one named exemption of R-KG.

decisions.subject: P67-11: R-LF
decisions.recommendation: A fixed merge-base range re-reports history; a gate reading its policy from the commit it judges can loosen itself. Rule text: The pre-push range is what git hands the hook on stdin (local ref, local sha, remote ref, remote sha), checked commit by commit (git rev-list --no-merges) with the APPROVED file of R-KX tested in each commit's parent tree; the policy in force for a commit is its BASE copy of the protected-paths file of R-LD (absent today), plus a short list hard-coded in the summary module that always shows raw diffs of the gate's own files.

decisions.subject: PR-68-1: R-LG
decisions.recommendation: PR-68-1 (the queue says only "committed JSON"). Rule text: The loop record is docs/reports/loop-records/[increment]/round-[nn].json (absent today), schema loop-record-v1, written only by the loop gate's run --write (create-exclusive, nn = highest + 1), never by hand and add-only; it keeps only what the gate cannot derive: schema, increment, round, decision (accept or revert), reason, accepted_findings, cases (id, status, got_sha), inputs (repo path to git blob id) and binding.

decisions.subject: PR-68-2: R-LH
decisions.recommendation: PR-68-2 (R-KI leaves this to the operator's pre-push reading). Rule text: The loop gate guards its own inputs mechanically (extends R-KI): the regression set only grows (no id is removed or moved to pending, and a group's count never falls; removal has one door, a ruling that resolves to a RATIFIED or RULED register row); OWED lines cannot worsen (R-LK); and hand-authored oracle files are not modified in a commit that changes code (R-LI).

decisions.subject: PR-68-3: R-LI
decisions.recommendation: PR-68-3 (d01e1458 moved oracle and code together). Rule text: Loop files fall in three classes: hand-authored ORACLE (expected answers, worked examples, invariants, floors, the regression set, prereg files and loop tests), never modified or deleted in a commit that also changes CODE, while adding a new oracle file beside code is allowed (red first); generated PINS (derived totals, id lists, records), which move only through the tool and only to the prereg totals; and CODE (catalogue, settings, switchboard, step, evaluator extension and Layer 2 model files, taken from the layer23 globs of the protected-paths file of R-LD); oracle-first is checked at commit when CODE or ORACLE is staged and over the range at push and in CI.

decisions.subject: PR-68-4: R-LJ
decisions.recommendation: PR-68-4 (closed set; one increment per round). Rule text: Increment ids are the closed set 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 6b, 7, 8, 9, 10 held in mcbylaws/loop/data/increments.json (absent today), copied from the queue's increments table; a round declares exactly one id in its prereg, and a catalogue row carries an increment field (MB-31 owns the row shape); no test locks the file to the queue file.

decisions.subject: PR-68-7: R-LK
decisions.recommendation: PR-68-7 (M-372 article 10.5.40 is the one OWED line today). Rule text: OWED floor lines are frozen at the value the round-0 ruling records: a further fall fails the gate (today an OWED line prints OWED and exits 0).

decisions.subject: G68-08: R-LL
decisions.recommendation: G68-08 and PR-68-5 (CI cannot see ~/Buildo-scratch/coa-data). Rule text: In CI the loop gate recomputes the in-repo groups only and prints "external groups: not run in CI"; groups whose data is held outside git (the CoA sets) are enforced at pre-push, which re-runs everything, and the content hash of each external data file is bound into the record's inputs; a --no-verify push therefore skips the external groups entirely, while CI still runs every data-free check (ratchets, floors-file edits, add-only records, oracle-first over the range, in-repo groups); if the data later moves into the repo, CI re-runs it.

decisions.subject: PR-68-8: R-LM
decisions.recommendation: PR-68-8 (R4-10 red evidence). Rule text: Every full loop run mutates one expected value in memory and requires the case to turn red (the red evidence of R-KU); the gate runs the canary itself and never stores it in the record.

decisions.subject: PR-68-9: R-LN
decisions.recommendation: PR-68-9 as amended (no second wiring path). Rule text: MB-68 delivers the loop gate's command line and exit codes and uses MB-67's protected-path globs and --mode (commit, push, ci); MB-67 alone wires the gate into the hooks and the workflow, through its external_arms entry, and the orchestrator makes it required in one commit after MB-68 lands.

decisions.subject: PR-68-10: R-LO
decisions.recommendation: PR-68-10 (queue O-14). Rule text: The loop gate computes rounds_since_thresholds (the rounds since the thresholds were last set, a revert counting) for the operator-card trigger O-14 and prints it; it is not stored in the record, and the card itself stays MB-27's.

decisions.subject: PR-68-11: R-LP
decisions.recommendation: PR-68-11 (measured). Rule text: The fast loop set, run at commit, is the in-repo groups plus the 172 set; the full set, run at push and in CI, is every group; both are cheap (the 172 scorer ran in 3.9 s on 2026-10-30).

decisions.subject: REASON-20: R-LQ
decisions.recommendation: CARD-wave0 section C, 20-character accept reason (R-BB and R-DA use the same minimum for their reasons). Rule text: A loop accept record carries a reason of at least 20 characters, and so does the reason of each accepted finding; a shorter reason fails the gate.
